# better-hermes-lcm v1.1.0-beta.1

First release of this fork. 122 commits on top of upstream `hermes-lcm` at `8d1b1e6`.

**This is a beta.** It has never run a real session — every number below comes from reading the
code and from a scripted end-to-end harness, not from an operator's `lcm.db`. Treat it as
something to try, not something to depend on.

## What the fork is for

Upstream keeps a summary DAG over a SQLite message store so a long conversation stays inside the
context window. This fork holds it to the promise in the name:

- **Nothing that reaches the plugin becomes unreachable.** Every stored row is either raw in the
  active context or reachable from a published summary node.
- **Anything removed from a view leaves a marker saying what went and how to get it back.** A
  bounded, capped, timed-out or failed operation is never reported as complete.
- **The tuning is weighted for the window it is actually running in**, not fixed at one size.

## The two changes that matter most

**Leaf chunking works at every window.** Upstream hands the whole backlog outside the fresh tail
to one summariser call, producing a single summary of everything — a one-shot compaction with a
DAG drawn around it. Compaction now produces one leaf per bounded chunk (4 % of the window) at
every window size, which is what makes `lcm_expand(node_id)` return a span a reader wanted rather
than hundreds of messages. Measured on the harness: 400 turns at a 256k window produce 12 leaf
nodes over 600 rows, where the same run previously produced 2 over 757.

**The retrieval tools no longer trim their own answers.** `lcm_recall` used to pop ranked hits off
a finished response until the JSON fit a character cap, rewriting `total_results` to the shortened
count — so the answer claimed there had never been more. `lcm_grep` stopped adding matches at a
cap with nothing in the body saying so. Both are gone, along with the clamps in `lcm_recent`,
`lcm_inspect` and `lcm_load_session`: `limit` is the caller's contract, and an oversized tool
response is the host's spillover problem, which the host already solves.

## Also in this release

- **A durable copy of host-spilled tool output.** Hermes writes an oversized tool result to its
  own cache and deletes it after 24 hours; the plugin keeps its own copy, so the archive does not
  end up holding a preview of something that no longer exists anywhere.
- **A fidelity contract in the summariser prompt.** The prompt said what a summary must cover and
  never what it must not invent. It now forbids inference, keeps hedges as hedges, and requires an
  unresolved thing to be named as unresolved — the one failure mode no marker can catch, because
  the node stays intact, expandable and honest about its sources while the text is wrong.
- **The skill tells the agent to expand before trusting a summary.** The recall policy injected
  into every turn was routing questions about the current conversation at `lcm_grep` — searching
  past the index instead of using it. It now says the summaries in context are an index, each
  carries its node id and an expand handle, and a load-bearing value is verified against the
  original.
- **Revision chains are followed to the original row.** Two edits of the same message left the
  original behind the frontier, covered by no node at all.
- **A summariser refusal is a refusal.** Upstream fell back to deterministic truncation; this fork
  raises instead, leaves the raw messages in context, and arms a cooldown.
- **Two levers cannot be switched on**, because either one can only put a reference in the replay
  the agent never saw.

## Known limitations

- **The weighting is frozen outside 256k–1M.** Below 256k every weighted value keeps its 256k
  number, which at a 32k window makes the fresh-tail cap larger than the whole window — the cap is
  then treated as absent and the session never compacts. Above 1M every value keeps its 1M number.
  Set `LCM_FRESH_TAIL_MAX_TOKENS` explicitly on a small window until this is fixed.
- **Condensation is unexercised by the harness.** It stubs the summariser, so the frontier never
  grows enough to trigger condensation and both anchors finish at depth 0. Everything above depth 0
  is verified by reading, not by running.
- **No real session has ever run.** See the first paragraph.

## Verification

```
python3 scripts/e2e_no_loss.py 262144 400      → 0 unreachable rows, 0 missing facts, 0 never offered
python3 scripts/e2e_no_loss.py 1000000 3000    → 0 unreachable rows, 0 missing facts, 0 never offered
```

## Install

```bash
git clone --branch v1.1.0-beta.1 --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/ConstantinLevin/better-hermes-lcm ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm
```

Then enable the plugin and the context engine in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`, and restart Hermes.
The database schema is unchanged from upstream `v1.0.0-rc.1`; the fork's own additions migrate
themselves on first open. There is no downgrade — take a copy of `lcm.db` first if you want one.
